faq.title: FAQ
faq.freeAnswer: Yes. Paseo is free and open source. You need agent providers installed with your own credentials. Voice is local-first by default and can optionally use cloud speech providers if you configure them.
faq.codeQuestion: Does my code leave my machine?
faq.codeAnswer: Paseo doesn't send your code anywhere. Agents run locally and talk to their own APIs as they normally would. For remote access, you can use the optional <relay>end-to-end encrypted relay</relay>, connect directly over your local network, or use your own tunnel.
faq.agentsAnswer: Paseo supports many providers. It has custom implementations for Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, OMP, Antigravity, and Muse Code, and supports many more via ACP. See the full list here: <agents>all supported providers</agents>. See <muse>Muse Code setup and limitations</muse>.
faq.providersAnswer: Paseo runs the providers installed on your machine as you'd normally run them. Paseo doesn't modify or change their behavior.
faq.desktopQuestion: Do I need the desktop app?
faq.desktopAnswer: No. You can run the daemon headless and use any client to connect. The desktop app just bundles the daemon with a UI.
faq.voiceAnswer: Voice runs locally on your device by default. You talk, the app transcribes and sends it to your agent as text. Optionally, you can configure OpenAI speech providers for higher-quality transcription and text-to-speech. See the <voice>voice docs</voice>.
faq.networkQuestion: Can I connect from outside my network?
faq.networkAnswer: Yes. You can use the hosted relay (end-to-end encrypted, Paseo can't read your traffic), set up your own tunnel (Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, etc.), or expose the daemon port directly. See <connectivity>connectivity</connectivity>.
faq.gitQuestion: Do I need git or GitHub?
faq.gitAnswer: No. Paseo works in any directory. Worktrees are optional and only relevant if you use git. You can run agents anywhere you'd normally work.
faq.banQuestion: Can I get banned for using Paseo?
faq.banAnswer: Paseo is designed to use each provider's officially supported integration and does not attempt to bypass its terms of service. It doesn't extract tokens or call inference APIs directly.
faq.worktreesAnswer: When you launch an agent with the worktree option (from the app, desktop, or CLI), Paseo creates a git worktree and runs the agent inside it. The agent works on an isolated branch without touching your main working directory. See the <worktrees>worktrees docs</worktrees>.

note.independent: Paseo is an independent project used by tens of thousands of developers daily.
note.maintained: It is maintained by one person, full time, and shaped by the community. There are no investors, no board and no company behind it. I have turned down funding offers to keep it that way.
note.community: The community helps Paseo grow through feedback, testing, bug reports, code contributions and plugins. Your sponsorship helps me keep improving and maintaining it.
note.neutral: A tool that sits between you and your code, your keys and your machines has to stay neutral, and that gets hard once someone else owns a return on it. Funding creates pressure to monetize, and that pressure changes what gets built.
note.selfFunded: Paseo is self-funded: the work is paid for by sponsorship and by <hub>Paseo Hub</hub>, an optional hosted service. Your support is what lets me keep working on it.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.whatAnswer: Paseo Hub is a separate service that sits above your Paseo daemons. Connect one or more daemons to automate agent runs from GitHub, Linear, Slack, Discord, schedules, and webhooks, and share them with your team. Paseo works on its own without Hub.
faq.separateQuestion: Why is Hub a separate service instead of part of the daemon?
faq.separateAnswer1: The daemon stays a single process on one machine. Hub talks to daemons over the same RPCs that the app and CLI use, so anyone can build another service on top of Paseo.
faq.separateAnswer2: Hub also has a different job. It receives public webhooks, handles team access, and runs multi-tenant. None of that belongs inside a single-machine daemon.
faq.selfHostAnswer: Yes. Run npx @getpaseo/hub or start it with Docker Compose and finish setup in your browser. The Apache 2.0 source is on GitHub, and the self-hosting guide covers production deployments.
faq.needQuestion: What do I need to run it?
faq.needAnswer: You need Node.js or Docker and a running Paseo daemon. Hub walks you through connecting your daemons and provider apps.
faq.hostedAnswer: Yes. The <hosted>hosted service</hosted> runs the same open-source Hub software that you can self-host. Hub dashboard members and pending invitations count as seats.
faq.codeQuestion: Can Hub run code on my machines?
faq.codeAnswer: Only on daemons where you grant the hub.execute permission. Enrolling a daemon does not enable execution by default, and you can revoke the permission from the machine at any time.
faq.moveQuestion: Do I have to move my team to a new tool?
faq.moveAnswer: No. Hub runs from GitHub, Linear, Slack, Discord, schedules, and webhooks on the daemons you already use. When you want to inspect or steer a run directly, open the live session in Paseo on desktop or mobile.
faq.agentsAnswer: Hub runs the providers configured on your connected Paseo daemons, including custom providers from plugins. Agents use the subscriptions, models, and skills on those machines.
faq.plannedIntro: These capabilities are not built yet, and are listed so you know where Hub is heading.

faq.accessAnswer: Self-host Hub with npx @getpaseo/hub or sign in to hosted Hub with a free account. Upgrade from Billing inside Hub when you need more runs or seats.
